Markets & Regulation

Wall Street Roars Back for Jensen Huang; Bitcoin Fades to $60,000 and an Eighty-Cent Rule

Nvidia’s board reversed itself after consulting Washington, sending the Nasdaq up 6.5%—while bitcoin gave back its $64,500 spike and the CFTC priced it at a 20% reserve haircut.

Eleven days after Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation and watched roughly $2.7 trillion evaporate from its October peak, directors consulted senior U.S. government officials, declared Huang no national-security risk, and unanimously reinstated him on Monday [s535, s334]. Equities erupted on cue: Nvidia surged roughly 32% to 35% in Monday trading, the S&P 500 snapped a seven-day slide with a nearly 5% jump, and by 09:30 CET Tuesday the Nasdaq Composite stood at 24,089.56, up 6.5% in a single session [s559, s568, s570].

Bitcoin did not stay for the party. After bouncing off a weekend low near $55,100 to briefly clear $64,500 on Monday morning, it surrendered nearly the entire rally within hours—sliding back to $61,100 by Monday afternoon and trading at $60,063.27, down 1.9%, at Roger’s 09:30 CET Tuesday snapshot [s541, s568, s570]. The round trip liquidated about $321 million in leveraged bitcoin positions ($224 million of them shorts) while the U.S. dollar index climbed to 104.40, its strongest level since April 2025, ahead of a December Fed meeting where a quarter-point rate hike remains the base case [s568].

On the same day, Washington wrote its own discount into the rulebook. CFTC Staff Letter 26-31, issued November 23, permits registered derivatives exchanges, swap execution facilities, and clearinghouses to count Bitcoin and Ether toward mandatory 12-month operating reserves—subject to a minimum 20% haircut and excluding the separate cash-or-securities liquidity floor [s553].

Bitcoin just crossed another line inside the U.S. regulatory perimeter, and the price is 20 cents on the dollar.

TFTC (News Bot) [s553]

Across the feed, reactions split between macro realism and dark humor. Bitcoin Well noted that Nvidia alone now accounts for roughly 8% of the S&P 500—leaving passive index savers riding on one executive’s personal life—while tuma joked that the whole sequence looked like pantomime to buy cheap Nvidia stock [s535, s304]. Jack Mallers dismissed the equity theater altogether, writing that as wild as all the jensen stuff is, what matters most to bitcoin is liquidity. [s279]. On CNBC Overtime, Blockstream CEO Adam Back took the longer view, calling bitcoin Ultimately it's improved gold. and arguing the market remains in the early innings of a bull cycle [s311].

Corporate balance sheets showed no consensus either. Strategy disclosed buying 457 BTC last week for $29.6 million (an average of $64,898 per coin), bringing its treasury to 851,305 BTC while also repurchasing $211.8 million in preferred shares [s556, s562]. Strive stood pat at 43,404 BTC, and miner Bitdeer sold all 281 BTC it mined last week to remain at zero [s561, s563]. Credit rails kept expanding anyway: Hut 8 subsidiary American Bitcoin locked in a $150 million revolving credit line from FalconX at 5.95% backed by reserves at Anchorage Digital Bank, and Cross River Bank launched its first bitcoin-backed consumer loans with LendingUSA [s554, s567].

Policy & Enforcement

Ukraine Advances Legalization 22–0; UK Bars Exchange Self-Trading

A Ukrainian parliamentary committee voted 22–0 to advance legislation legalizing bitcoin and crypto, taxing net gains at the standard personal income rate with a temporary 5% rate through 2028 for existing holdings [s284]. Committee deputy chair Yaroslav Zhelezniak said parliament could vote this week, targeting a July 1, 2027 start pending passage and presidential sign-off [s284]. In London, the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority moved to bar crypto exchange operators from market making against their own customers on their own venues [s565].

Custody & Seizures

DOJ Moves on $1.1B in USDC as BitMart Discloses a $319.5M Hole

The U.S. Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint (Case No. 1:26-cv-04150) on November 23 seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC across 36 addresses on 18 blockchains tied to North Korea’s $6.34 billion Binance hack—a reminder, TFTC noted, that The government's enforcement power runs through Circle's killswitch, not Bitcoin's ledger. [s556]. Elsewhere, centralized exchange BitMart disclosed a $319.5 million balance-sheet shortfall against $1.9 million in liquid assets, leaving over 12 million accounts frozen after marketing 18.8% annualized yield products days before halting trading [s557].

Privacy Beat

Signal Blocks AI Screenshots; Oyster Breach Hits 265,000

Signal now blocks screenshots by default to stop OS-level AI agents from reading chats, while 265,000 London Oyster photocard holders learned their home addresses and birth dates had been exposed [s80, s86]. Coincards.com summed up the lesson bluntly: Every database is a breach on a timer. Give them less. [s86]. The same account warned users never to obey Pump.fun’s prompt to paste private keys into a website [s73].

Protocol, Cryptography & Infrastructure

Research, releases & node operations
Cryptography

Praxis Shrinks Witness Encryption to 8 GB, With One Catch

Writing on the new Praxis paper (eprint.iacr.org/2026/2971) co-authored by David Tse, waxwing called the scheme’s general witness encryption at an 8 GB ciphertext size a steep drop from the ~100 TB order of magnitude in PIPEsv2—it's a truly groundbreaking result assuming nothing is fundamentally wrong. [s205].

Where Tse’s earlier BABE proposal unlocked a single UTXO with a valid zero-knowledge proof, Praxis aims at general witness encryption [s205]. Yet in a follow-up note, waxwing flagged an unaddressed flaw: the paper does not consider a dishonest encryptor who encrypts garbage, leaving a decryptor with a valid ZKP still unable to claim funds—a problem BABE solved with a compact cut-and-choose garbled circuit that may not scale here [s201].

Node Software

Core Patches AI-Found Stall; Floresta Ships SwiftSync

Bitcoin Core disclosed and patched CVE-2026-117348 in versions 30.5, 31.3, and 32.1 after an automated LLM scan from Block’s Spiral (Project Loupe) caught a duplicate-inv orphan-transaction stall that could freeze a node for over a dozen seconds per message [s564]. Operators still on end-of-life 29.x builds must upgrade [s564].

Meanwhile, Utreexo-based full node Floresta released v0.10.0 with SwiftSync for faster initial block download, stronger validation, JSON-RPC authentication, and broader Bitcoin Core RPC compatibility [s68, s544]. On the hardware side, BitcoinBrabant began offering a home router built on open RISC-V hardware running StartWRT with per-security-profile networks [s195].

Lightning

BOLT12 Pay Adds Phoenixd; Watchtowers Under Review

Alex71btc⚡💜₿🚀 rolled out a major BOLT12 Pay update adding Phoenixd support alongside LND + LNDK, letting self-hosted operators switch backends while keeping Offers, wallet assignments, payment history, and NWC links intact [s58, s530]. The release also brings CSV export for bookkeeping, improved BIP353 and LNURL flows, Android Companion deep links, and session revocation on password change [s58].

Elsewhere on Lightning, A Rux 🚴🏿 polled node runners on whether watchtowers are still worth the maintenance after their StartOS rust-teos plugin crashed twice this month, noting Eclair skips towers in favor of a 720-block delay and asking whether a longer window plus downtime alerts is enough for home nodes [s455].

Nostr Pulse & Field Notes

P2P markets, relay hygiene & grassroots education
Peer-to-Peer

Mostro Marks Four Years With 4,700 Orders and a New App

Four years after its first commit on November 23, 2022, Mostro—born out of Telegram’s lnp2pBot to eliminate single points of failure—now spans 11 trusted Mostros across Latin America and Europe [s29]. Since January 2026, the network has logged more than 4,700 completed orders and over 500 million sats traded across 47 currencies, with half of all disputes resolved in roughly 20 minutes, verifiable at mostro.world [s29]. Its new desktop and mobile app is live on Zapstore and GitHub [s28].

Network & Governance

Relay Hygiene, Regex Spam Traps, and a Guild Debate

JeffG publicly flagged a misconfiguration on the Damus relay—where inbox events can be sent but NIP-42 authentication fails with a missing serviceUrl error—and delivered a blunt checklist for relay operators: set up alerts, verify auth, and keep lists trim [s180, s236]. You have agents now, you have no excuses. Either run a good service or shut it down responsibly. [s236].

To cope with Global feed junk, Po shipped regex filtering in client settings and argued that 1 to 3 targeted rules catch 99% of current spam without risking client hangs [s543, s545]. Meanwhile, the launch of The Freedom Guild drew praise from 𝙰𝚉𝙾𝚁 🥷 as a value-for-value alliance for builders and writers, but immediate skepticism from Hugh Janus: Freedom needs open networks, not closed clubs. [s233, s379]. In a reflective essay, Constant urged builders to stop waiting for a TikTok-style viral explosion and accept a quieter winter of steady groundwork [s277].

Education & Adoption

Proof-of-Work Hardware Grants and Circular Economies

My First Bitcoin published its latest Impact Report: fully funded for 2026, under budget through October, with 66% of spending directed into educational programs and eight months of runway to July 2027 [s7]. Blockstream is now using the group’s public proof-of-work leaderboard to route donated Jade Classic hardware wallets to active teaching communities [s5, s302].

In South Africa, BitcoinEkasi took its Bitcoin Diploma students in Mossel Bay to spend Lightning rewards via Bolt cards at The Meat Station [s171]. And ahead of next week’s conference in Malawi, Fedi highlighted BitMsika, a Fedi Mini App that settles Lightning payments directly into Malawian kwacha on local mobile-money networks [s16].
